title: Preserve fragment links when <base> is defined

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

labels.name: topic: url
labels.description: URL parsing in documents, base URLs and the base element

body:
Currently, links pointing to a fragment — e.g. `<a href="#some-id">` — are resolved with the `<base>`, triggering a request to the base URL with the fragment attached. While this seems technically _expected_, this seems realistically _unexpected_.

* [MDN Citation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/base#in-page_anchors)

My understanding is that a lone fragment is typically used to link to sections or content in the current document, or to act as a nil reference for JavaScript side effects. My understanding is that a `<base>` href typically defines a _base_ URL applied to multiple pages or assets, and is often _not_ the target document itself.

If that understanding is accepted, it seems incorrect to apply the base href to a fragment link.

Could this expectation be changed, or could some functionality be added to allow HTML authors the ability to prevent fragment links from inheriting the base URL?

_Note_: In testing, I noticed that [internal fragments work as expected in Safari (v14.0 & v14.2)](https://codepen.io/embed/prefill?editable=true&default-tab=html%2Cresult&data=%7B%22html%22%3A%22%3Cbase+href%3D%5C%22https%3A%2F%2Fgoogle.com%5C%22+%2F%3E%5Cn%5Cn%3Ca+href%3D%5C%22%23gbqfbb%5C%22%3E%5Cn%5CtTake+me+down.%5Cn%3C%2Fa%3E%5Cn%5Cn%3Cp+id%3D%5C%22gbqfbb%5C%22+style%3D%5C%22margin-top%3A100vh%5C%22%3E%5Cn%5CtTo+the+paradise+city.%5Cn%3C%2Fp%3E%22%7D), but only when the base href points to another origin.
